Live from NPR News in New York City, I'm Dua Lisa Kautau. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky
says it is unfortunate that President Trump just signed an executive order to temporarily
exempt Russia from economic sanctions already passed by Congress. The news comes as Russia

Congresswoman Ilhan Omar are demanding the Justice Department return all properties seized by federal
agents in a search of her Minnesota home this week. In pairs Ryan Lucas reports they also say
the investigation targeting Omar is politically motivated. In a letter to the Justice Department,
Omar's attorneys called the investigation a vindictive, retributive, and politically motivated
effort to go after one of President Trump's chief critics in Congress. They point out that
the court-authorized search of Omar's home in Washington, D.C. took place just weeks before
the midterm elections, which violates a longstanding Justice Department norm that aims to avoid taking
action that could be perceived as interfering in an election. Federal agents seized Omar's phone,
computer, and documents during their search of her home as part of an investigation into possible
immigration fraud. Omar was born in Somalia and came to the U.S. as a child. Her attorneys say
there is no legitimate basis to suggest that Omar violated any law concerning her citizenship status.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News. Pope Leo is back home at the Vatican
four days after surgery for lung cancer. Megan Williams is in Rome with the latest.
The 71-year-old American Pope walked out of Rome's Jamely Hospital on his own Saturday afternoon,
waving to well-wishers and stopping to greet a 13-year-old Ukrainian girl being treated for cancer.
Doctors say his latest blood tests and chest scans look good. Leo had the lower lobe of his
right lung removed Tuesday after doctors confirmed adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.
He's due back in St. Peter's Square Sunday to give the weekly Angelus blessing,
his first public appearance since surgery. The Vatican says plans are still moving ahead
for his November trip to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru. For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
The Holy Father plans to deliver his weekly prayer tomorrow, but Vatican officials say he is not
expected to receive a private audience for now. You're listening to NPR News from New York City.
A critically endangered frog in Ghana has been successfully bred in captivity.
Conservationists hope the feed could help save a super tiny and extraordinary species,
and Piers Ari Daniel reports. An adult Afia Barago's puddle frog can easily fit on your
thumbnail. A mining project is threatening the frog's habitat, which could wipe them out.
So a group called Herp Conservation Ghana and the London Zoo teamed up to collect some frogs to rear
in captivity. Zoo keeper Unar Iverson says the frogs have reproduced and there are now at least
15 froglets. It's very hard when you have next to no knowledge on that species. I'm just over the
moon and we're really optimistic about what their future kind of holds. If the mind goes through,
the team could take what they've learned in London to Ghana to perhaps relocate the frogs to a
compatible habitat nearby, which they hope might protect the species from extinction. Ari Daniel,
NPR News. Another attack in the occupied West Bank today. This time the violence targeted
European diplomats and Catholic representatives on an official visit. A French mayor described
the ordeal in a Facebook post saying he was struck with metal bars and kicked to the ground
by several masked individuals with quote extreme aggressiveness. A day earlier, Washington Post
veteran photojournalist Heidi Levine was filmed getting beaten by mass settlers as she reported on
